source_refs.note: Topic 30.7, as printed (PDF 212). The CDCl₃ signal printed 'near 80 ppm' is marked; a Book correction gives about 77 ppm.

blocks.text: The nucleus of ¹²C does not have magnetic properties because of even number of protons and neutrons (even mass number), and is, therefore, NMR inactive. However, the ¹³C nucleus possesses magnetic spin due to its odd number of neutrons. On the basis of the magnetic properties of carbon-13 isotope, ¹³C NMR spectra can be recorded for carbon compounds. Like ¹H NMR, chemical shift (δ in ppm) in ¹³C NMR is compared to the reference molecule TMS (δ = 0.0 ppm). However, the ¹³C NMR has a range of chemical shift from 0 – 220 ppm. The deuterated chlorofom (CDCl₃) is usually used as a solvent which produces a small signal near 80 ppm.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The ¹³C signal of CDCl₃ is near 77 ppm (a 1:1:1 triplet centred at 77.16 ppm), not 80 ppm.
